events.summary: Captured the user-directed exploratory honeycomb-slot WorkflowCanvas design. No canvas implementation is authorized by this record.
Activated as the ongoing design ledger while the interaction model and inspiration prototype are developed.
Confirmed Workbench as the sole future integration seam: a prop-compatible honeycomb canvas will replace the existing WorkflowCanvas element without duplicating workflow state or callbacks.
Added an isolated, query-selectable honeycomb prototype backed by the real sample workflow shape; production Workbench and production canvas remain unchanged.
Confirmed the local honeycomb preview renders the slot lattice and three sample nodes; a slot selection applies its selected state and the browser reported no console errors.
Changed the prototype node from a rounded rectangle to an inset hexagon and reduced its unframed image from 45px to 38px.
Expanded the active todo into explicit objective-and-acceptance checkpoints for every documented slot, node, drag, path, and canvas state.
Set both slot and node hex perimeters to 4px, preserving a separate 4px slot-to-node gap.
Replaced the CSS-clipped slot boundary layers with one SVG polygon per slot, preserving the 4px perimeter and CSS hover/selection treatments.
Added hexagonal clipping layers for slot and node content; the node now keeps its article semantics with an SVG outline as its first child.
Verified the local preview exposes 35 slot boundaries, three node boundaries, and matching hex clip containers without browser console errors.
Corrected node centering to the 4px slot inset and layered the clipped fill beneath a single visible SVG perimeter.
Reworked the live 18px node inset as centered regular-hex geometry, separated grid gap terminology, and made the prototype slot markup valid within its button.
Verified regular node geometry in the local preview and passed Studio build and lint; lint reports only pre-existing fast-refresh warnings outside the prototype.
Moved prototype geometry authority to CSS custom properties, deriving slot height from side length and having TypeScript read resolved values for axial layout and SVG geometry.
Adjusted the CSS-to-TypeScript geometry bridge to use a hidden probe's resolved dimensions because direct custom-property reads retain calc tokens in the browser.
Verified the CSS-owned geometry chain resolves correctly in the local preview; all 35 slots render and the browser reports no console errors.
Added each workflow node ID to the top-right end of the node flat edge as a secondary visual identifier.
Verified the node ID labels render at the intended top-right placement in the local preview with no browser console errors.
Added a test-page-only r-005 placeholder in the upper axial slot between r-001 and r-002, leaving shared sample workflow data unchanged.
Verified r-005 renders in axial slot q:1,r:0 between r-001 and r-002 with no browser console errors.
Recorded the next slot visual grammar: a non-interactive outer SVG hexagon supplies sharp, dashed, muted, transparent gridlines around the interactive slot button.
Implemented the passive outer gridline frame in the prototype and verified all 35 gridlines are transparent, dashed, mitered, pointer-inert SVG polygons while slot selection remains clickable.
Changed the layout to a gapless logical honeycomb: each frame is inset 4px with a 1px passive perimeter, while its node remains separately inset by a further 4px with a 4px perimeter.
Reverted the outer slot-frame experiment at the user's direction. The prototype returns to its pre-frame interactive slot boundary as the clean baseline for a new approach.
Reintroduced the frame with separated axial placement: the existing slot dimensions are the outer frame, grid gap is the regular inner-slot inset, and the node derives from that inner slot.
Changed the passive outer slot-frame perimeter from dashed to solid at the user's direction.
Made the frame the CSS geometry root. Its standard side, width, and height drive axial placement and the frame SVG; the slot side is now calculated from the frame side and slot inset.
Added a session-resume handoff with the live frame hierarchy, verification boundary, worktree safety constraints, and immediate visual-QA step.
Recorded connection ports as the proposed semantic and visual edge-attachment model; their geometric anchor coordinates will support shortest compatible path routing.

Refined the edge-attachment model: fixed lattice anchors, one at every logical cell edge midpoint and corner, remain independent of shrinkable visual frames; node ports bind semantic capabilities to those anchors.

Corrected the port model: each slot owns six dedicated side ports at fixed nominal-frame coordinates. Neighboring ports intentionally stack at shared positions; close-up presentation may fan and curve their paths without changing logical endpoints.

Started the stacked-port prototype slice: removed sample edge rendering, generated six passive slot-port markers per logical frame, and separated nominal port geometry from grid-gap-driven visual frame shrinkage. Studio build passed; visual marker QA remains pending after the desktop preview connection timed out.
A fresh local honeycomb preview confirmed six passive side ports per slot, visually stable co-located neighboring ports, and no rendered workflow paths. Port-marker refinement remains active.
Moved each of the six slot-owned port markers from side midpoints to nominal frame vertices, where three honeycomb frames meet. Studio build and fresh visual preview verification passed.
Created child design record 2026-09-02-workflow-canvas-port-routing to settle stable stacked-port identities and path-routing policy before restoring paths.
Implemented readable slot, junction, and slot-port identifiers in the isolated prototype. Paths remain absent; Studio build passed.

Verified 210 generated port IDs are unique across the 35-slot prototype and that a canonical junction groups three distinct slot owners. Studio lint passed with only three pre-existing fast-refresh warnings.
Restored visible sample workflow paths in the isolated prototype as bright direct vertex-port routes with directional arrow markers.
Fresh local preview visibly showed Manual Trigger to Set System Volume to Search Solo Leveling routes. Studio build and lint passed; lint retained only three pre-existing warnings.
Superseded the dashed-arrow route styling at the user's direction. Direct routes now use plain solid high-contrast cyan lines, without glow or directional decoration.
Fresh local preview confirmed plain solid routes remain visibly distinct from frame perimeters. Studio build and lint passed; lint retained only three pre-existing warnings.
Moved prototype r-004 from slot/q4-r-1 to the user-directed slot/q4-r2. Its direct r-002 to r-004 route recomputes from the placement bridge.
Studio build passed and a fresh isolated preview exposed Search Solo Leveling only at slot/q4-r2, with its direct route exiting toward that lower placement.
Replaced the prototype's direct route shortcut with complete traversals over its slot-owned ports, shared junction transfers, and adjacent frame edges.
Studio build and lint passed. The isolated preview shows routes following port-to-port frame geometry; lint retained only three existing warnings outside the prototype.

Reviewed the Honeycomb canvas, slot, and node snapshot renderers. Marked the renderer-consumed baseline transports for canvas idle, node execution idle, node connection isolated, and path flow idle complete; state-specific visual and interaction objectives remain active.
